name: Sugar Land
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Sugar Land, TX 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Sugar Land, TX: free Santa photos at Town Square, Holiday Lights at Constellation Field, Cookies with Santa and a Polar Express day.
lede: Sugar Land celebrates Christmas around Town Square, where the city lights its tree and Santa poses for free photos, with a big light show at Constellation Field and holiday days at the city's museums.
celebrates: Christmas in Sugar Land centers on Sugar Land Town Square. Sugar Land Parks and Recreation hosts the annual Christmas Tree Lighting there, with letters to Santa, hot chocolate, face painting and performers on the main stage, plus free parking at Mercer Stadium and shuttles to the square. Town Square then brings Santa back on Saturday afternoons for complimentary photos. At Constellation Field, Sugar Land Holiday Lights fills the ballpark with millions of lights, Santa photos and a carnival. Indoors, HMNS at Sugar Land serves cookies with Santa and Mrs. Claus, the Fort Bend Children's Discovery Center plans themed holiday days, and Smart Financial Centre books holiday shows. Nearby Richmond lights its tree at City Hall Park Plaza on December 4 and the George Ranch Historical Park serves S'mores with Santa on December 12, and Stafford hosts Holiday on the Plaza at SMSD Plaza on December 12.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Sugar Land listed its Christmas Tree Lighting for Friday, December 5, at Sugar Land Town Square, as part of a yearly event calendar that also included Fall Fest on the square in September. Local news reported the 2025 lighting would run from 5 to 8 pm at 2711 Plaza Drive. Sugar Land Parks and Recreation also invited families to make time for photos with Santa at that tree lighting.
facts: Sugar Land really is named for sugar. The Williams brothers opened a raw sugar mill on their Oakland Plantation in 1843, and in the early 1900s the town became a company town for the Imperial Sugar Company. The last sugarcane crop in Fort Bend County was harvested in 1928, after which the refinery imported raw sugar. Sugar Land was not incorporated as a city until 1959, and T. E. Harmon was its first mayor.
trains: Railroads helped build Sugar Land. In the 1850s, plantation owners Benjamin F. Terry and William J. Kyle helped extend the Buffalo Bayou, Brazos and Colorado Railway through the property. In the 1890s, E. H. Cunningham built the fourteen mile Sugar Land Railroad, with Sugar Land as one of its stations, and later owners ran it alongside their sugar business. For a train outing today, the Rosenberg Railroad Museum next door keeps Tower 17 and historic rail cars, and the Galveston Railroad Museum runs a Christmas train.

kidfact: Sugar Land is named after real sugar. More than 100 years ago, farmers here grew sugarcane, and a big factory turned it into the sugar people put in their cookies.
faq: Where is the Sugar Land Christmas tree lighting?

The City of Sugar Land holds its annual Christmas Tree Lighting at Sugar Land Town Square, 2711 Plaza Drive. The city lists letters to Santa, hot chocolate, face painting and performers on the main stage. Free parking is available at Mercer Stadium, 16403 Lexington Boulevard, with shuttles running to Town Square during the event.
Where can kids see Santa for free in Sugar Land?

Sugar Land Town Square hosts Photos with Santa on Saturday afternoons in late November and December, and its page says the photos are complimentary. Each family gets up to five minutes with Santa. The visits are a partnership between Town Square, the City of Sugar Land and the SL4B Corporation.
What is Sugar Land Holiday Lights?

Sugar Land Holiday Lights is a ticketed light show at Constellation Field, the ballpark in Sugar Land. It features millions of lights, two themed areas, Santa photos, a carnival, a synthetic ice rink, mini golf and vendors. Tickets are sold online, and the show runs from late November into early January.
Why is it called Sugar Land?

The town grew up around sugar. The Williams brothers built a raw sugar mill on Oakland Plantation in 1843, and Sugar Land later became a company town for the Imperial Sugar Company. Sugarcane farming in Fort Bend County ended in 1928, but the refinery kept making sugar from imported raw sugar.
Are there trains near Sugar Land?

Sugar Land grew along railroads, including the Buffalo Bayou, Brazos and Colorado Railway and the fourteen mile Sugar Land Railroad built in the 1890s. Families who love trains can visit the Rosenberg Railroad Museum next door, with Tower 17 and historic rail cars, or the Galveston Railroad Museum.
